expanded_order.status: fail: one required defect (orphaned candle-lighting heading and kindling instruction); the requested pre-sunset and after-nightfall behaviour is otherwise correct
findings: Pre-sunset Friday, Elul 29 (checked from the condition expressions, not the old report). The outer gate (lines 356–374) is any(hebrew-date 6/29, rosh-hashana=1), so it is true. Weekday variant (lines 380–420): branch A needs Elul 29 and none(secular-day 6), which is false on Friday; branch B needs rosh-hashana=1, which is false. So the weekday variant is hidden. Shabbat variant (lines 427–444): all(Elul 29, secular-day 6) is true. No ancestor carries a j:declare: the Minchah declaration closes at line 309, the eruv declaration at line 351, and neither section contains the lights. The Shabbat variant itself has no declaration, so no automatic actual-day gate can hide it. The extraction has no internal conditional, so all its words appear. The runtime agrees for 2026-09-11 15:00 Minchah: shabbat_light=true, english_ordinary_light=0, eruv=false, refrains=0.

After nightfall on RH-Shabbat (Hebrew date Tishrei 1, civil date still Friday). The Shabbat variant needs Elul 29, so it is false. Weekday branch B needs shabbat=false, so it is false, and branch A needs Elul 29, so it is also false. No blessing appears, as intended. Kabbalat (lines 454–467) needs shabbat=true and maariv=true, and both hold, so Psalms 95–99 and 29, Lekhah Dodi with 11 refrains, Psalms 92 and 93, and the gated Mourner's Kaddish are all present. None of them has omission logic. The runtime agrees for 2026-09-11 22:00: shabbat_light=false, refrains=11, mourner_kaddish=true. This is full Kabbalat, consistent with the confirmed different custom.

findings.evidence: The outer festival_lights gate is any(Elul 29, rosh-hashana=1). It is broader than the union of its two variants. The heading 'הדלקת נר של יום טוב / Festival lights' (lines 376–377) and the instruction 'The housewife kindles the festival lights and says the following benediction:' (line 378) sit outside both variant gates. So whenever rosh-hashana=1 but neither variant applies, they appear with no blessing after them. That happens on (a) RH-Shabbat after nightfall, which is exactly the rh_shabbat_night case: the page tells the reader to kindle lights on Shabbat and then gives nothing; and (b) every RH1 non-Maariv compile, including the book's own RH1 Shacharit build, where a lighting heading and instruction appear before section_morning. The verification JSON counts only blessings, never this heading or instruction, so 'passed' does not cover the problem.
findings.required_fix: Make the outer gate exactly any(weekday-variant condition, Shabbat-variant condition). That is: any(all(Elul 29, none(secular-day 6)), all(rosh-hashana=1, shabbat=false, maariv=true), all(Elul 29, secular-day 6)). Change it in readings.json expanded_order festival_lights.conditions and regenerate. Then add verification observations for the lights heading or instruction (absent in rh_shabbat_night and in an RH1 Shacharit case; present in the before-sunset, weekday-night and undated cases).

findings: Weekday variant coverage is correct. Elul 29 on Monday, Wednesday or Thursday before sunset shows the ordinary blessing (runtime 2024-10-02 15:00 and 2025-09-22 15:00: english_ordinary_light=1, shabbat_light=false). RH1 weekday Maariv shows the ordinary blessing (2024-10-02 22:00). Elul 29 can never fall on Saturday, so none(secular-day 6) leaves no gap.

The undated build shows both variants, each with its own condition rubric ('כשיום טוב אינו בשבת:' and 'לפני כניסת שבת, כשיום טוב חל בשבת:'). The runtime agrees: shabbat_light=true and english_ordinary_light=1.

Behaviour to note, not a defect: a congregation that brings in Shabbat early on Friday and builds with maariv=true before sunset gets no Kabbalat, because the shabbat aggregate is still false. In the same build the combined-blessing branch stays visible. This follows from the confirmed incoming-Maariv design.

limits: I ran no compiler, validator or tests. The runtime outcomes come only from /tmp/mahzor-kabbalat-verification.json, which records booleans and counts: refrains, eruv, mourner_kaddish, shabbat_light, english_ordinary_light. It records no heading or instruction presence and no compiled word sequence. So it neither confirms nor rules out the orphaned heading, and it does not show the compiled Shabbat blessing text. My word-for-word check is file against file.

The verification JSON contains no runtime caveat field, and no case covers twilight (between sunset and nightfall on Friday), RH1 Shacharit, or an early Friday Maariv. Behaviour at twilight depends on how the runtime treats an undefined Hebrew date and is unverified.

I assumed opensiddur:day-of-week secular-day=6 means civil Friday. I base that on the user's statement and on the before-sunset case returning shabbat_light=true for 2026-09-11. I did not re-read features.yaml.
I read only the last six prayer.jsonl records (lines 23286–23291). I did not check whether kind 'variant' is in the registry checker's allowed kind list.

I did not re-check the unchanged leaves (eruv files, psalm leaves, English index) beyond confirming that the Heidenheim and English hadlaqat leaves still carry only the ordinary wording. Image-level source fidelity rests on the frozen final audit.
